items.claim: Argument comparison now builds, sorts and prints a synthetic object for both fields on every pair, dropping the old zero-cost paths for no-argument fields and differing argument counts, with no per-node caching.
items.consequence: A ~3KB query `{ f f f ... }` with 1500 repeated no-arg fields compares ~1.1M pairs, each now calling `print()` twice; validating it with this rule alone took ~18s in a scratch mocha run. In a micro-benchmark, 200k comparisons of two no-arg fields took 7298ms with the new code versus 10ms with the old logic, and `f(a: 1)` vs `f(a: 1, b: 2)` took 22776ms versus 1.6ms. This is a validation-time DoS amplification on a rule that is already quadratic.

items.claim: Order-insensitivity of arguments now depends on `naturalCompare` giving a strict order, but it returns 0 for distinct names whose long digit runs collide in float precision, so the stable sort keeps source order and the printed strings differ.
items.consequence: `{ f(a12345678901234567890: 1, a12345678901234567891: 2) f(a12345678901234567891: 2, a12345678901234567890: 1) }` is valid (same arguments, different order), but a scratch run at head reports 'Fields "f" conflict because they have differing arguments'. The old code looked arguments up by exact name, so it was order-independent for any names.

items.claim: Results for documents with duplicate argument names change silently and no test is added or updated to pin the new semantics.
items.consequence: At head, `{ f(a: 1, a: 2) f(a: 1, a: 2) }` reports no conflict and `{ f(a: 1, a: 1) f(a: 1, b: 2) }` reports 'differing arguments'; the old first-match-by-name logic gave the opposite result in both cases. A commit titled 'simplify' therefore changes which errors users see alongside UniqueArgumentNames errors, and nothing in the test file covers it.

items.claim: Arguments are compared by fabricating a fake `ObjectValueNode` and comparing its printed text, which ties rule correctness to the printer's object formatting and `sortValueNode` internals instead of comparing arguments structurally.
items.consequence: Maintenance cost: any later change to `print` for ObjectValue, or to `sortValueNode` ordering, silently changes validation results. A name-keyed `Map` of `args2` with per-value comparison would be the more robust fix for the old `find` scan and would keep the cheap early exits.

items.claim: `stringifyArguments` recomputes the same string for a field node every time that node appears in a pair, with no memoization.
items.consequence: A field with arguments that appears in N overlapping selections is printed O(N) times per node (O(N²) prints overall), where a `WeakMap<FieldNode, string>` cache or a length/empty pre-check would bring this back to O(N) prints. In the micro-benchmark, identical two-argument fields were ~3x slower than before (34469ms vs 11770ms per 200k comparisons).
